bindings.caption: Clean FTO in detergent solution using ultrasonic bath. Bath temperature, detergent composition and concentration are unreported. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.
Rinse with water and ethanol. Rinse with water and ethanol Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

Immerse FTO in 40 mM aqueous TiCl4 at 70 °C. Teflon container; compact transparent TiO2 layer. Bath volume and TiCl4 hydrolysis speciation unreported. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.
Wash coated FTO with water and ethanol. Wash coated FTO with water and ethanol Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

Load substrate and 15 mL precursor mixture into Teflon container. Teflon container placed in stainless-steel autoclave; capacity, fill fraction and closure geometry not specified. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

Grow vertically aligned TiO2 rods at 150 °C for 4 h. Hydrothermal process. Pressure, ramp, cooling and TiO2 crystal phase not specified in this article; cited reference title is not imported as phase evidence. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

Immerse again in 40 mM TiCl4 at 100 °C for 1 h. Second TiCl4 treatment; aqueous identity established for initial bath but not separately restated here. Bath volume and subsequent rinse not supplied. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

Anneal composite TiO2 film at 450 °C for 1 h. Annealing atmosphere, equipment and ramps are not specified. Apparatus dimensions, liquid level and spatial layout are schematic, not measured source geometry.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
